newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers meets with Zairean rebels. [Corrected 14:36 gmt]
newsitem.headline: De Beers meets with Zairean rebels. [Corrected 14:36 gmt]

text.p: South African diamond giant De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd said on Monday its representatives had met with Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila at the weekend. (Corrects to show de Beers representatives met Kabila in person, not his representatives).
De Beers said it had buying offices in the Zaire towns of Kisangani and Mbuji-Mayi and a contract to buy the production of the Miba mine at Mbuji-Mayi.
Kabila's rebel forces, battling to oust ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko, now control both these towns.
"De Beers can confirm that its representatives met with Mr Kabila over the weekend to discuss its concerns relating to the protection of its staff and facilities," the firm said in a statement.
Miba is 80 percent owned by the Zaire government with Sibeka of Belgium owning the remaining 20 percent. De Beers holds 20 percent of Sibeka and so has a minor indirect stake in the Miba mine.

On Monday news broke of a rebel advance to within 30 km of the crucial mining centre and second largest city of Lubumbashi. Zairean army soldiers in Lubumbashi have now put on white headbands to symbolise that they have switched support to the rebel forces of Laurent Kabila.

The rebels took up arms in October in a dispute over Zairean nationality for ethnic Tutsis and have vowed to topple Mobutu, who has rarely been in the country since undergoing prostate cancer surgery in Europe in August.
The rebels control almost a third of the mineral-rich but chronically poor central African country.
